evidence_quotes.agenda: 'do you have any other specific concerns or what are your major stresser for this upcoming, anything you'd like to share?' — asked, but only after the full address/inventory probe.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer raised a real concern — 'I'm just seeing if we're going to be able to afford it, they've gotten some quotes before and they're pretty high' — and got a single answer (straight into rate/minimum) with no further digging into what 'pretty high' meant to him.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'you'd really save money and time with the moving company if you do that, we'll keep your costs down' (self-prep tip, delivered early re: pre-loading boxes); no other Sheet 5 lines land before the call ends.

top_strength: Clean quid pro quo open with an explicit time estimate ('this may take five to ten minutes').
coaching_note: Customer flags an affordability worry directly and the call goes straight to the rate/minimum without ever reaching a personalized hours estimate — he says 'it's a little too high' before Amy gets to anchor a range, so the estimate step (and the reassurance in Save Your Ass) never happens.
